hook: Unsafe hostels ignore HYDRAA's *3-month* move-out warning
hook_b: Unsafe hostels ignore HYDRAA's *3-month* move-out warning
tldr: After a seven-storey illegal hostel building collapsed at Anjaiah Nagar, Gachibowli in August killing two workers, HYDRAA told operators to shift to safe buildings within three months. Many have not, Telangana Today reports; inspections start January 1.

beats.what: Several hostel managements in Hyderabad and Cyberabad have not vacated unsafe premises or added safety measures despite HYDRAA's warning.
beats.why: HYDRAA Commissioner AV Ranganath gave the warning after the August collapse at Anjaiah Nagar, Gachibowli.
beats.care: If you live in a PG/hostel: check stairs, exits and ventilation; HYDRAA says buildings at risk of collapse will be demolished after Jan 1 inspections.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Telangana Today (Nov 18): residents describe rooms shared by 2-4 people, narrow staircases, undersized lifts and choked vents.

cards.q: Does your hostel/PG have a second exit?

qs: Where would residents go if many hostels shut at once?
Who checks fire exits in hostels before January?

facts.t: Operators say they hold leases of *1-3 years* paid in lakhs, so they won't move.

viz.verdict: Deadline nears with many hostels unchanged

steps.e: 7-storey hostel building collapses, Anjaiah Nagar; 2 workers dead
HYDRAA: shift to safe buildings in 3 months

watch: HYDRAA's inspections from January 1 and whether any hostels are sealed or demolished.

sources.name: Telangana Today
sources.title: HYDRAA warning fails to move unsafe hostels in Hyderabad

fact: Hyderabad hostels are ignoring HYDRAA's *three-month* deadline to leave unsafe buildings
twist: Operators say they signed 1-3 year leases worth lakhs and complying could shut hostels across the city.
